grammar_and_binders: S.12 otchs + shedor explicitly introduce x and recipient r as dislocated topics; S.13 resumes them with or and sodaiiin.

A fronted chey + event phrase may scope forward across a physical line break to an explicitly written predicate in the same S paragraph. The first guard attaches to shedy (adhesion), not to itself or a hidden process.
Participant binders bind x to the initial nutriment and r to the initial recipient; explicit anaphoric forms are used in each later clause. No default or image-selected owner is supplied.
The final qodaiin event is an explicit attraction process; its chey guard attaches to that event and is followed by the explicit orar event phrase.
The trailing chy in S.13 coordinates the following written presentation clause; it is not silent punctuation.

complete_working_reading: Nutriment x at receiving part r remains adherent until assimilation completes. It adheres at that part, and it had been presented there before the adhesion. Its continued withdrawal away from that part prevents adhesion and full assimilation. The attractive faculty draws that same nutriment toward that same part until presentation/arrival there completes.

source_departures: The target's strict UNTIL guard is read as cessation at the assimilation/presentation boundary. Galen III.1 does not explicitly state that retention ceases exactly at assimilation, and the presentation-as-goal statement alone does not establish the same strict target operator.
The target supplies no written teleological argument; the source's purposeful-Nature premise is not imported into the paragraph.
The uncertain ZL string chz[s:r] receives a provisional exact-form value. IT/RF alternatives ch?s and ch@152;s are not aliases and remain unassigned.
assumption_ledger.counting_note: Twenty-one additional exact whole-form values cover the other twenty-one ZL types. This is a maximally costly exploratory lexicon, not evidence of lexical economy. Same exact values are preserved globally wherever those exact literal forms recur.

rival_after_chey.changed_item_only: chey is AFTER the completion of the same supplied event, with all other values, participants and attachments held fixed.
rival_after_chey.before_consequence: The adhesion event is constrained to finish at assimilation completion; the attraction/drawing event is constrained to finish at presentation/arrival completion.
rival_after_chey.after_consequence: The same adhesion event is placed after assimilation completion, and the same attraction event is placed after presentation/arrival completion.
rival_after_chey.comparison: In the proposed source-constrained model, AFTER reverses both temporal boundary consequences and conflicts with III.1's stage ordering/presentation-as-goal account. These are consequences of fixed assumed meanings, not an observed Voynich time contrast; the target strings do not independently reveal the event order.
